```python
def _headers(venue: str, method: str, path: str, query: str, tr_id: str | None,
             public: bool) -> tuple[dict, dict | None, str | None]:
    """(headers, json_body, token) for one attempt, built afresh each time; each keys.read names exactly
    CREDENTIALS[venue], and a public path reads no key. Never the demo-trading header (E3)."""
    if public:
        return {"Accept": "application/json"}, None, None
    if venue == "kis" and method == "POST":
        app_key, app_secret = keys.read(CREDENTIALS["kis"])
        return ({"content-type": "application/json; charset=utf-8"},
                {"grant_type": "client_credentials", "appkey": app_key, "appsecret": app_secret}, None)
    if venue == "kis":
        token = _kis_token()
        app_key, app_secret = keys.read(CREDENTIALS["kis"])
        return ({"content-type": "application/json; charset=utf-8", "authorization": f"Bearer {token}",
                 "appkey": app_key, "appsecret": app_secret, "tr_id": tr_id, "custtype": "P"}, None, token)
    if venue == "upbit":
        access_key, secret_key = keys.read(CREDENTIALS["upbit"])
        return ({"Authorization": f"Bearer {_upbit_jwt(access_key, secret_key, query)}",
                 "Accept": "application/json"}, None, None)
    api_key, secret, passphrase = keys.read(CREDENTIALS["okx"])
    timestamp = _okx_timestamp(_clock())
    return ({"OK-ACCESS-KEY": api_key,
             "OK-ACCESS-SIGN": _okx_sign(secret, timestamp, path + ("?" + query if query else "")),
             "OK-ACCESS-TIMESTAMP": timestamp, "OK-ACCESS-PASSPHRASE": passphrase,
             "Content-Type": "application/json"}, None, None)


def _date(headers) -> datetime | None:
    """The answer's Date header (its name in any case) as an aware UTC datetime; None when absent or unreadable."""
    value = next((v for k, v in headers.items() if k.lower() == "date"), None)
    try:
        moment = parsedate_to_datetime(value)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None
    if moment.tzinfo is None:                         # "-0000": UTC with no local zone given (RFC 5322)
        moment = moment.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    return moment.astimezone(timezone.utc)


class _TokenRejected(InquiryError):
    """A KIS inquiry answered with one of KIS_TOKEN_CODES: request marks the token it sent bad."""


_CODE = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9_]{1,40}")           # a venue code worth naming in an error text; nothing else is


def _check_answer(venue: str, path: str, status: int, body_bytes: bytes) -> object:
    """E15: the parsed body of an HTTP 200 answer that carries the venue's success marker (KIS rt_cd "0", or a
    non-empty access_token from the token POST; OKX code "0"; Upbit no error key). A KIS inquiry answered with a
    token code (on any status) raises _TokenRejected; HTTP 401 or 403, or a code in AUTH_CODES[venue], AuthError;
    anything else, a 3xx included, InquiryError. Each text names the venue, the path, the HTTP status and the
    venue's code only: never a message, a header or the body (E37)."""
    try:
        body, parsed = json.loads(body_bytes), True
    except ValueError:                                # not JSON, or not UTF-8: the bytes are never quoted
        body, parsed = None, False
    code = _code(venue, body)
    text = f"{venue} {path}: HTTP {status}" + (f" {code}" if code else "")
    if venue == "kis" and path != KIS_TOKEN_PATH and code in KIS_TOKEN_CODES:
        raise _TokenRejected(text)
    if status in (401, 403) or code in AUTH_CODES[venue]:
        raise AuthError(text)
    if status == 200 and parsed and _succeeded(venue, path, body):
        return body
    raise InquiryError(text if parsed else f"{text}: not JSON")


def _code(venue: str, body: object) -> str:
    """The venue's own code in a parsed body (KIS msg_cd, or the token answer's error_code; OKX code; Upbit
    error.name); "" when there is none or it is not a short plain word."""
    if not isinstance(body, dict):
        return ""
    if venue == "kis":
        raw = body.get("msg_cd") or body.get("error_code")
    elif venue == "okx":
        raw = body.get("code")
    else:
        raw = body["error"].get("name") if isinstance(body.get("error"), dict) else None
    return str(raw) if raw is not None and _CODE.fullmatch(str(raw)) else ""


def _succeeded(venue: str, path: str, body: object) -> bool:
    """The venue's success marker in a parsed HTTP 200 body (E15)."""
    if venue == "upbit":
        return not (isinstance(body, dict) and "error" in body)
    if not isinstance(body, dict):
        return False
    if venue == "okx":
        return body.get("code") == "0"
    if path == KIS_TOKEN_PATH:
        return isinstance(body.get("access_token"), str) and body["access_token"] != ""
    return body.get("rt_cd") == "0"


def _b64url(raw: bytes) -> str:
    """base64url without padding, as a JWT part."""
    return base64.urlsafe_b64encode(raw).rstrip(b"=").decode("ascii")


def _upbit_jwt(access_key: str, secret_key: str, query: str) -> str:
    """The Upbit JWT (research upbit.md 2): HS512 over the base64url header and payload with the secret used raw;
    the payload holds access_key and a fresh uuid4 nonce, plus query_hash (the SHA512 hex of `query`, the exact
    string sent in the URL) and query_hash_alg when there is a query. No exp claim."""
    payload = {"access_key": access_key, "nonce": str(uuid.uuid4())}
    if query:
        payload |= {"query_hash": hashlib.sha512(query.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest(), "query_hash_alg": "SHA512"}
    signing_input = ".".join(_b64url(json.dumps(part, separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8"))
                             for part in ({"alg": "HS512", "typ": "JWT"}, payload))
    signature = hmac.new(secret_key.encode("utf-8"), signing_input.encode("ascii"), hashlib.sha512).digest()
    return f"{signing_input}.{_b64url(signature)}"


def _okx_timestamp(moment: datetime) -> str:
    """OK-ACCESS-TIMESTAMP: ISO 8601 UTC with milliseconds (truncated) and Z, for example 2026-10-24T00:00:00.000Z."""
    return moment.astimezone(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%f")[:-3] + "Z"


def _okx_sign(secret: str, timestamp: str, request_path: str) -> str:
    """OK-ACCESS-SIGN (research okx.md 2): Base64 of HMAC-SHA256(secret, timestamp + "GET" + the request path with
    its query + an empty body)."""
    message = (timestamp + "GET" + request_path).encode("utf-8")
    return base64.b64encode(hmac.new(secret.encode("utf-8"), message, hashlib.sha256).digest()).decode("ascii")


def _kis_token() -> str:
    """The KIS bearer token for one GET attempt (spec 5 "Token"): the cached one while it is not bad and now <
    expires_at - 120 s; else one issue through the token POST, at most once per 70 s per process. The folder, the
    cache and the temp file pass checked_target BEFORE the POST and before the 70 s starts, so a refused target
    sends nothing and burns no issuance (a refusal propagates: a crash, E33). KIS answers the same token for 6
    hours, so a token it had called bad that the POST hands back is AuthError and blocks issuing for 6 hours."""
    global _next_issue_at
    path = isolation.state_root() / "kis_token.json"
    now = _clock().timestamp()
    cached = _read_token(path, now)
    if cached is not None and cached not in _bad_tokens:
        return cached
    if _next_issue_at is not None and now < _next_issue_at:
        raise InquiryError("kis: no token may be issued yet; KIS skipped this poll")
    checked_target(path.parent, "KIS token folder")
    checked_target(path, "KIS token cache")
    tmp = checked_target(path.with_name(f".kis_token.{os.urandom(6).hex()}.tmp"), "KIS token temp")
    _next_issue_at = now + TOKEN_MIN_GAP_S
    answer = request("kis", "POST", KIS_TOKEN_PATH)
    token = answer.body["access_token"]
    if token in _bad_tokens:
        _next_issue_at = now + TOKEN_REISSUE_BLOCK_S
        raise AuthError("kis: KIS issued a token it had called invalid; no token for 6 hours")
    _write_token(path, tmp, token, now + float(answer.body.get("expires_in") or 86400))
    return token


def _read_token(path: Path, now_epoch: float) -> str | None:
    """The cached token when `path` holds a non-empty access_token and now_epoch < expires_at - 120 s (the quote
    client's reuse rule); None for a missing, unreadable or malformed file or a token that is about to expire."""
    try:
        data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        token, expires_at = data["access_token"], float(data["expires_at"])
    except (OSError, ValueError, TypeError, LookupError):
        return None
    return token if isinstance(token, str) and token and now_epoch < expires_at - TOKEN_REUSE_MARGIN_S else None


def _write_token(path: Path, tmp: Path, token: str, expires_at: float) -> None:
    """{"access_token", "expires_at"} (epoch seconds; the quote client's format) written atomically: to `tmp`, the
    temp name checked before the POST, opened exclusively and fsynced, then os.replace onto `path`, each target
    checked again just before it is used. An OSError propagates (a crash, E33): the next poll finds the old cache,
    or none, and may issue once the 70 s have passed. A write that fails after the open leaves its uniquely named
    temp file behind (nothing here deletes a file); it is never read or reused, and the next issue (KIS hands back
    the same token within 6 hours) writes a fresh one."""
    checked_target(path.parent, "KIS token folder").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with open(checked_target(tmp, "KIS token temp"), "x", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write(json.dumps({"access_token": token, "expires_at": expires_at}))
        fh.flush()
        os.fsync(fh.fileno())
    os.replace(checked_target(tmp, "KIS token temp"), checked_target(path, "KIS token cache"))
```

  `test_aggregator_skips_missing_and_isolates_broken_modules` checks the module-level imports).

**Plan decisions used:** E4 (canonical JSON, sha256 hex, the copied sidecar lock with fsync), E16 (the snapshot
fields: settled fiat `cash`, coins as holdings, `deposit_krw`, the recent-window lists), E17 (`STALE_AFTER`, read by
Task 8), E30 with E1R2-4 (daily `inquiry-YYYYMMDD.jsonl` files under one `inquiry.lock`; `read_all`, no
`read_since`), E33 and E38 (a refused write propagates as a crash), E37 (`FieldError(name)`; error and `load` texts
from names only), E39 (`clock_offset_s`), E42 (the `code_unsigned` flag); contract sections 0.5, 3.2 and 8.

Design notes (read before Step 3):
- Three points refine section 8 where it is silent; none renames anything. (1) `write_lines` opens `"a+b"` where
  section 8 writes `"ab"`: the same handle reads the last byte to isolate a torn line, and append mode still puts
  every byte at the end (owner.py's lock file is opened the same way); the 0.5 guard accepts it, since the first
  argument of that `open()` is a call of `checked_target`. (2) `__post_init__` makes `flags` a frozenset and
  refuses a venue or flag outside the lists, and `load` refuses a row whose keys are not exactly the fields (an
  extra key would ride along unhashed) or that is not the row `dump` writes for the record it rebuilt (`dict()` and
  `tuple()` would otherwise turn `""`, `[]` or a list of pairs into a valid container and a dict `flags` into its
  keys; the hash binds only the rebuilt values, so such a row changes no value, but it is not a line E1 wrote); all
  raise `ValueError` with names-only text, so E37 and E38 hold. The comparison runs inside the same `try` as the
  rebuild, so any error in it is reported the same way.
  (3) `load` turns a `RecursionError` into `ValueError`: measured on the venv (Python 3.13.14), `json.loads` reads
  2,998 nested objects while `model.jsonable` stops near 1,000, so a forged deep row that `read_all` returns would
  otherwise escape Task 11's `checks._load`, which catches `LookupError`, `TypeError`, `ValueError` and
  `AttributeError` only. No ledger ruling is needed for these: they are this plan's own text.
- Snapshots carry no clock: `utc` is the poll's `now` that the caller passes in, and the Seoul date that picks the
  daily file is computed by the poller (Task 12). This module reads no clock, no key and no network.
- `checked_target` judges only the last component of a path, so `write_lines` alone would write through a junction
  folder; every caller writes inside an `exclusive()` on the same folder (contract 16.2 steps 3, 4 and 7, 16.4),
  and `exclusive` judges that folder first. The junction test writes the way the poller does.
- Every test writes only under the suite's temp home: `_t4_root()` refuses any state root whose folder name does not
  start with `tradegen_home_` before a file is written, so calling a test function outside the wrapper writes
  nothing to the real `~/.tradegen`. The two link tests compute their paths first (so the state-root link scan runs
  on a clean root and is memoised) and make the link after, as tests/compliance_owner.py:568-584 does; they prove
  that `checked_target` itself refuses, not the scan.

```python
def snap(venue: str, **fields) -> "Snapshot":
```

```python
"""Snapshot records and the JSONL helpers (E1 plan Task 4; spec 4 "State files", 6 "Snapshot"; E4, E16, E30, E37).

Every test runs inside tests.execution_acceptance._wrap (hermetic, a temp TRADEGEN_HOME, the refusing send) and
writes only under that temp home: `_t4_root()` refuses any other state root before a file is written. Helpers are
prefixed `_t4_` so that a later task appending here cannot shadow them.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
import dataclasses
import hashlib
import inspect
import json
import os
import threading
from datetime import date, timedelta
from pathlib import Path

from core.compliance import model
from execution import snapshot as S
from tests import execution_fixtures as F
from tests.notrun import NotRun

_T4_VICTIM = b"another file's bytes: E1 never writes them\n"
_T4_ADDRESS = "bc1qfixtureaddress000000000000000000000"
_T4_KEYS = ("cash", "clock_offset_s", "deposit_krw", "deposits", "earn", "error", "fills", "flags", "holdings",
            "key_expiry", "loans", "ok", "open_orders", "prices_krw", "response_sha256", "server_utc",
            "snapshot_sha256", "utc", "venue", "withdrawal_addresses", "withdrawals")   # contract 8, sorted


def _t4_root() -> Path:
    """The suite's temp TRADEGEN_HOME (tests.compliance_fixtures.temp_home names it tradegen_home_*). Any other root
    is refused before a file is written, so a direct call outside the wrapper never touches ~/.tradegen."""
    root = Path(os.environ.get("TRADEGEN_HOME") or "")
    if not root.name.startswith("tradegen_home_"):
        raise AssertionError(f"not inside the suite's temp home: {root}")
    assert S.home() == root / "execution", S.home()
    return root


def _t4_listing(root: Path) -> list[str]:
    """Every path under `root`, relative and sorted."""
    return sorted(p.relative_to(root).as_posix() for p in root.rglob("*"))


def _t4_raises(call, kind: type[Exception] = ValueError) -> str:
    """The message of the `kind` exception `call()` raises; AssertionError when it raises none."""
    try:
        call()
    except kind as exc:
        return str(exc)
    raise AssertionError(f"no {kind.__name__} raised")


def _t4_refused(call, needle: str) -> None:
    """`call()` must raise checked_target's RuntimeError, whose text names `needle`."""
    text = _t4_raises(call, RuntimeError)
    assert needle in text, text


def _t4_full() -> S.Snapshot:
    """An ok Upbit-shaped snapshot with every field set away from its default."""
    return F.snap(
        "upbit", server_utc="2026-10-24T00:00:01Z", clock_offset_s=1.0,
        holdings={"BTC": S.Holding(units=0.0001, locked=0.0, avg_cost=100_000_000.0)},
        cash={"KRW": 20_000.0}, deposit_krw=21_000.0,
        open_orders=(S.Order(id="u-open-1", symbol="BTC", side="buy", units=0.0001, price=90_000_000.0),),
        fills=(S.Move(id="u-done-1", symbol="BTC", counter="KRW", side="buy", units=0.0001),),
        deposits=(S.Move(id="u-dep-1", symbol="KRW", side="in", units=20_000.0),),
        withdrawals=(S.Move(id="u-wd-1", symbol="BTC", side="out", units=0.0001),),
        withdrawal_addresses=(S.Address(currency="BTC", net_type="BTC", address=_T4_ADDRESS),),
        key_expiry="2027-05-27T06:17:51Z", loans={"loan_amt": 0.0}, earn={"savings": 0.0},
        flags=frozenset({"EVENTS"}), prices_krw={"BTC": 100_000_000.0, "USDT": 1_400.0},
        response_sha256={"/v1/accounts": "a" * 64})


# field -> a value other than _t4_full()'s; a nested record changes one inner field
_T4_ALT = {
    "venue": "kis", "utc": "2026-10-24T00:05:00Z", "server_utc": "2026-10-24T00:00:02Z", "clock_offset_s": 2.0,
    "ok": False, "error": "upbit: /v1/accounts: field balance",
    "holdings": {"BTC": S.Holding(units=0.0001, locked=0.00005, avg_cost=100_000_000.0)},
    "cash": {"KRW": 20_001.0}, "deposit_krw": None,
    "open_orders": (S.Order(id="u-open-1", symbol="BTC", side="buy", units=0.0001, price=90_000_001.0),),
    "fills": (S.Move(id="u-done-1", symbol="BTC", counter="USDT", side="buy", units=0.0001),),
    "deposits": (), "withdrawals": (S.Move(id="u-wd-2", symbol="BTC", side="out", units=0.0001),),
    "withdrawal_addresses": (S.Address(currency="BTC", net_type="BTC", address=_T4_ADDRESS, secondary_address="m"),),
    "key_expiry": None, "loans": {"loan_amt": 1.0}, "earn": {}, "flags": frozenset({"EVENTS", "okx_perm"}),
    "prices_krw": {"BTC": 100_000_001.0, "USDT": 1_400.0}, "response_sha256": {"/v1/accounts": "b" * 64},
}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# The records and their hash

def test_snapshot_sha256_is_the_hash_of_every_other_field():
    s = _t4_full()
    body = json.loads(S.dump(s))
    stored = body.pop("snapshot_sha256")
    text = json.dumps(body, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False)
    assert stored == s.snapshot_sha256 == hashlib.sha256(text.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
    assert _t4_full().snapshot_sha256 == s.snapshot_sha256                   # stable: same fields, same hash
    assert dataclasses.replace(s, snapshot_sha256="0" * 64).snapshot_sha256 == s.snapshot_sha256   # never supplied
    assert len(s.snapshot_sha256) == 64 and set(s.snapshot_sha256) <= set("0123456789abcdef")


def test_snapshot_sha256_changes_with_every_field():
    names = {f.name for f in dataclasses.fields(S.Snapshot)} - {"snapshot_sha256"}
    assert set(_T4_ALT) == names, sorted(names ^ set(_T4_ALT))              # a new field needs a case here
    base = _t4_full()
    seen = {base.snapshot_sha256}
    for name, value in _T4_ALT.items():
        assert getattr(base, name) != value, name
        changed = dataclasses.replace(base, **{name: value})
        assert changed.snapshot_sha256 not in seen, name
        seen.add(changed.snapshot_sha256)


def test_non_finite_numbers_are_refused():
    nan, inf = float("nan"), float("inf")
    builds = (
        lambda: F.snap("kis", deposit_krw=nan),
        lambda: F.snap("kis", cash={"KRW": inf}),
        lambda: F.snap("kis", clock_offset_s=-inf),
        lambda: F.snap("okx", loans={"liab": nan}),
        lambda: F.snap("okx", earn={"savings": inf}),
        lambda: F.snap("upbit", prices_krw={"BTC": nan}),
        lambda: F.snap("upbit", holdings={"BTC": S.Holding(units=inf)}),
        lambda: F.snap("upbit", holdings={"BTC": S.Holding(units=1.0, avg_cost=nan)}),
        lambda: F.snap("kis", open_orders=(S.Order(id="o", symbol="005930", side="buy", units=1.0, price=inf),)),
        lambda: F.snap("kis", fills=(S.Move(id="f", symbol="005930", side="buy", units=nan),)),
        lambda: S.failed("kis", "2026-10-24T00:00:00Z", "kis: x", clock_offset_s=nan),
    )
    for n, build in enumerate(builds):
        assert "finite" in _t4_raises(build), n
    line = S.dump(_t4_full())
    assert b'"KRW":20000.0' in line and b"NaN" not in line
    row = json.loads(line.replace(b'"KRW":20000.0', b'"KRW":NaN'))           # json.loads reads NaN; load must not
    assert row["cash"]["KRW"] != row["cash"]["KRW"]
    assert _t4_raises(lambda: S.load(row)) == "snapshot row: ValueError"

    assert S.FLAGS == frozenset({"keys_missing", "code_unsigned", "auth_error", "okx_perm", "okx_acct_lv",

        line = S.dump(s)

        assert line == (model.canonical_json(s) + "\n").encode("utf-8")

def test_load_rebuilds_every_record_and_round_trips():
    snaps = [_t4_full(), F.snap("kis"), F.snap("okx", flags=["okx_perm", "EVENTS"]),

def test_a_tampered_row_is_refused_and_the_text_names_no_value():
    good = json.loads(S.dump(_t4_full()))

    def edited(change) -> dict:
        row = json.loads(json.dumps(good))
        change(row)
        return row

    deep = json.loads('{"a":' * 2000 + "123456" + "}" * 2000)              # json reads it; jsonable cannot recurse
    tampered = [
        edited(lambda r: r["cash"].update(KRW=123456.0)),                    # a value changed, the hash kept
        edited(lambda r: r.update(ok=False)),
        edited(lambda r: r.update(snapshot_sha256="0" * 64)),
        edited(lambda r: r.update(extra=123456)),                            # a field the record does not have
        edited(lambda r: r.pop("error")),
        edited(lambda r: r.update(holdings={"BTC": [123456]})),
        edited(lambda r: r["open_orders"][0].update(note="123456")),
        edited(lambda r: r.update(fills="123456")),
        edited(lambda r: r.update(flags=["EVENTS", "nope"])),
        edited(lambda r: r.update(cash=[["KRW", 123456.0]])),
        edited(lambda r: r.update(cash=deep)),
        [good],
        "123456",
    ]
    for n, row in enumerate(tampered):
        text = _t4_raises(lambda r=row: S.load(r))
        assert text.startswith("snapshot row: ") and "123456" not in text, (n, text)
    assert _t4_raises(lambda: S.load(tampered[-3])) == "snapshot row: RecursionError"
    assert S.load(good) == _t4_full()
    empty = json.loads(S.dump(S.failed("kis", "2026-10-24T00:00:00Z", "kis: x")))
    two = json.loads(S.dump(F.snap("okx", flags={"EVENTS", "okx_perm"})))
    look_alikes = [                                     # the values are unchanged, so the hash still recomputes
        edited(lambda r: r.update(cash=[["KRW", 20000.0]])),
        edited(lambda r: r.update(earn=[["savings", 0.0]])),
        edited(lambda r: r.update(flags={"EVENTS": 0})),
        edited(lambda r: r.update(flags=["EVENTS", "EVENTS"])),
        dict(two, flags=["okx_perm", "EVENTS"]),
        dict(empty, deposits=""), dict(empty, withdrawals={}), dict(empty, open_orders={}),
        dict(empty, prices_krw=""), dict(empty, earn=[]), dict(empty, loans=[]),
    ]
    for n, row in enumerate(look_alikes):
        assert _t4_raises(lambda r=row: S.load(r)) == "snapshot row: not canonical", n
    assert S.load(empty) == S.failed("kis", "2026-10-24T00:00:00Z", "kis: x")
    assert S.load(two).flags == frozenset({"EVENTS", "okx_perm"})

def test_paths_live_under_the_state_root_and_computing_them_creates_nothing():
    root = _t4_root()
    before = _t4_listing(root)
    assert S.inquiry_path(date(2026, 10, 24)) == root / "execution" / "inquiry-20261024.jsonl"
    assert S.inquiry_path(date(2026, 10, 24)).name == "inquiry-20261024.jsonl"
    assert S.inquiry_path(date(2027, 1, 5)).name == "inquiry-20270105.jsonl"
    assert S.read_all(S.inquiry_path(date(2026, 10, 24))) == []                # a missing file reads as []
    S.write_lines(S.inquiry_path(date(2026, 10, 24)), [], "E1 inquiry log")   # no lines: nothing opens
    assert _t4_listing(root) == before and not S.home().exists()
    assert not hasattr(S, "read_since")                                        # E30: the daily files replace it


def _t4_order(guard, wait: float) -> list[str]:
    """The order in which two threads pass through `guard()`: A gets in first, then waits up to `wait` s for B."""
    order: list[str] = []
    a_in, b_in = threading.Event(), threading.Event()

    def a() -> None:
        with guard():
            order.append("a-in")
            a_in.set()
            b_in.wait(wait)                    # under a real lock B cannot get in, so this wait times out
            order.append("a-out")

    def b() -> None:
        a_in.wait(5)
        with guard():
            order.append("b-in")
            b_in.set()

    threads = [threading.Thread(target=a), threading.Thread(target=b)]
    for t in threads:
        t.start()
    for t in threads:
        t.join(30)
    assert not any(t.is_alive() for t in threads), "a thread is stuck"
    return order


def _t4_os_locked(lock: Path) -> bool:
    """True when a second, read-only handle cannot take the byte lock of `lock` (another process would not)."""
    with open(lock, "rb") as fh:
        try:
            if os.name == "nt":
                import msvcrt
                msvcrt.locking(fh.fileno(), msvcrt.LK_NBRLCK, 1)
                fh.seek(0)
                msvcrt.locking(fh.fileno(), msvcrt.LK_UNLCK, 1)
            else:
                import fcntl
                fcntl.flock(fh, fcntl.LOCK_SH | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
                fcntl.flock(fh, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
        except OSError:
            return True
    return False


def test_exclusive_serialises_two_threads_and_holds_an_os_lock():
    path = _t4_root() / "execution" / "probe.jsonl"
    assert _t4_order(contextlib.nullcontext, 5) == ["a-in", "b-in", "a-out"]  # control: without a lock B gets in
    assert _t4_order(lambda: S.exclusive(path), 0.5) == ["a-in", "a-out", "b-in"]
    lock = path.parent / "probe.jsonl.lock"
    assert lock.is_file() and not path.exists()                               # only the lock file is made
    with S.exclusive(path):                             # both locks: the OS lock alone also serialises two threads
        assert _t4_os_locked(lock) and S._LOCK.locked()
    assert not _t4_os_locked(lock) and not S._LOCK.locked()


def test_append_lines_isolates_a_torn_last_line():
    path = _t4_root() / "execution" / "rows.jsonl"
    S.append_lines(path, [b'{"a":1}\n'], "probe")
    assert path.read_bytes() == b'{"a":1}\n' and (path.parent / "rows.jsonl.lock").is_file()
    with open(path, "ab") as fh:
        fh.write(b'{"b":')                                                    # a crash in the middle of a line
    S.append_lines(path, [b'{"c":3}\n', b'{"d":4}\n'], "probe")
    S.append_lines(path, [b'{"e":5}\n'], "probe")                              # ends in a newline: none added
    assert path.read_bytes() == b'{"a":1}\n{"b":\n{"c":3}\n{"d":4}\n{"e":5}\n'
    assert S.read_all(path) == [{"a": 1}, {"c": 3}, {"d": 4}, {"e": 5}]
    S.write_lines(path, [], "probe")
    assert path.read_bytes().endswith(b'{"d":4}\n{"e":5}\n')
    assert "os.fsync(fh.fileno())" in inspect.getsource(S.write_lines)       # E4: every append is fsynced


def test_read_all_keeps_file_order_and_skips_unreadable_lines():
    path = _t4_root() / "mixed.jsonl"
    path.write_bytes(b'{"n":1}\n' + b'not json\n' + b'[1,2]\n' + b'"text"\n' + b'\xff\xfe{}\n' + b'\n'
                     + b"[" * 100_000 + b'\n' + b'{"n":2}\r\n' + b'{"n":3,"x":{"y":[1]}}\n' + b'{"n":')
    assert S.read_all(path) == [{"n": 1}, {"n": 2}, {"n": 3, "x": {"y": [1]}}]
    assert S.read_all(_t4_root() / "missing.jsonl") == []


def test_two_seoul_days_land_in_two_files_under_one_lock_file():
    root = _t4_root()
    late = F.snap("kis", utc="2026-10-23T14:59:59Z")                          # 23:59:59 KST on 23 October
    early = F.snap("kis", utc="2026-10-23T15:00:00Z")                         # 00:00:00 KST on 24 October
    with S.exclusive(S.home() / "inquiry"):
        S.write_lines(S.inquiry_path(date(2026, 10, 23)), [S.dump(late)], "E1 inquiry log")
        S.write_lines(S.inquiry_path(date(2026, 10, 24)), [S.dump(early)], "E1 inquiry log")
    assert sorted(p.name for p in (root / "execution").iterdir()) == [
        "inquiry-20261023.jsonl", "inquiry-20261024.jsonl", "inquiry.lock"]
    assert [S.load(r) for r in S.read_all(S.inquiry_path(date(2026, 10, 23)))] == [late]
    assert [S.load(r) for r in S.read_all(S.inquiry_path(date(2026, 10, 24)))] == [early]


def test_a_hard_linked_target_is_refused_and_nothing_is_written():
    root = _t4_root()                                   # the state-root link scan runs now, on a clean root
    day = S.inquiry_path(date(2026, 10, 24))
    day.parent.mkdir()
    victim, lock_victim = root / "victim.jsonl", root / "lock_victim"
    victim.write_bytes(_T4_VICTIM)
    lock_victim.write_bytes(_T4_VICTIM)
    os.link(victim, day)
    os.link(lock_victim, S.home() / "evidence.jsonl.lock")
    line = S.dump(F.snap("kis"))

    def under_the_inquiry_lock() -> None:
        with S.exclusive(S.home() / "inquiry"):
            S.write_lines(day, [line], "E1 inquiry log")

    def under_a_linked_lock() -> None:
        with S.exclusive(S.home() / "evidence.jsonl"):
            raise AssertionError("the hard-linked lock file was opened")

    _t4_refused(under_the_inquiry_lock, "hard link")
    _t4_refused(lambda: S.append_lines(day, [line], "E1 inquiry log"), "hard link")
    _t4_refused(under_a_linked_lock, "hard link")
    _t4_refused(lambda: S.append_lines(S.home() / "evidence.jsonl", [line], "E1 evidence log"), "hard link")
    assert victim.read_bytes() == lock_victim.read_bytes() == _T4_VICTIM
    assert not (S.home() / "evidence.jsonl").exists()


def test_a_junction_folder_is_refused_and_nothing_is_written():
    try:

    except ImportError:
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

  Create `execution/snapshot.py` (whole file, LF). It imports only `__future__`, `contextlib`, `dataclasses`,
  `json`, `os`, `threading`, `collections.abc`, `datetime`, `pathlib`, `msvcrt` or `fcntl` (inside `exclusive`),
  `core.compliance` and `core.isolation`, all on the 0.5 allowlist. It holds no `getattr`, no attribute assignment
  and no `object.__setattr__` outside `__post_init__` (Task 2's `_path_hits`). If you touch a docstring, write the
  word "canonical" in lower case only: test_09 and T-RO-01 match the KIS account-field text case-sensitively, and
  the upper-case spelling of that word contains it (0.5).

```python
"""One normalised, hashed record per venue per poll (E1 spec 6 "Snapshot"; plan E4, E16, E30, E37), the daily
inquiry files, and the sidecar lock and JSONL helpers every E1 state file uses (spec 4 "State files").

Paths are computed at call time under `core.isolation.state_root()/"execution"`, so a test's TRADEGEN_HOME moves
them; computing one creates nothing. Every write goes through `checked_target` just before it opens, the lock file
included. No clock, no key and no network: the poller passes the time in."""
from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
import dataclasses
import json
import os
import threading
from collections.abc import Iterator, Mapping, Sequence
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import date, timedelta
from pathlib import Path

from core.compliance import model
from core.isolation import checked_target, state_root

VENUES = ("kis", "upbit", "okx")
STALE_AFTER = timedelta(minutes=15)                 # an older snapshot gives no live positions (spec 6, E17)
FLAGS = frozenset({"keys_missing", "code_unsigned", "auth_error", "okx_perm", "okx_acct_lv", "okx_spot_borrow",
                   "okx_auto_loan", "okx_no_ip", "EVENTS", "derivative_position"})   # code_unsigned: KIS only, E42


class FieldError(ValueError):
    """A response field is missing or malformed. args[0] is the field's name, a literal of the parser; never its
    value (E37)."""


@dataclass(frozen=True, kw_only=True)
class Holding:
    units: float                          # total held, locked included
    locked: float = 0.0
    avg_cost: float | None = None         # in the venue's quote currency, where the venue gives one


@dataclass(frozen=True, kw_only=True)
class Order:
    id: str
    symbol: str
    side: str                             # "buy" | "sell"
    units: float
    price: float | None = None


@dataclass(frozen=True, kw_only=True)
class Move:
    """A fill, a deposit or a withdrawal."""
    id: str
    symbol: str
    counter: str = ""
    side: str                             # "buy" | "sell" | "in" | "out"
    units: float


@dataclass(frozen=True, kw_only=True)
class Address:
    currency: str
    net_type: str
    address: str
    secondary_address: str = ""


@dataclass(frozen=True, kw_only=True)
class Snapshot:
    """One venue at one poll (spec 6). `flags` is made a frozenset; snapshot_sha256 is always derived from every
    other field. A venue outside VENUES, a flag outside FLAGS or a number that is not finite is ValueError."""
    venue: str
    utc: str                              # the poll's now, model.iso_utc
    server_utc: str | None = None         # the venue's time (first Date header; OKX public/time), model.iso_utc
    clock_offset_s: float | None = None   # venue time minus the PC clock at receipt of that answer (E39)
    ok: bool
    error: str | None = None              # names, paths and codes only (E37)
    holdings: Mapping[str, Holding] = field(default_factory=dict)
    cash: Mapping[str, float] = field(default_factory=dict)          # fiat currency -> settled amount (E16)
    deposit_krw: float | None = None      # KIS dnca_tot_amt (D16 evidence); None elsewhere
    open_orders: tuple[Order, ...] = ()
    fills: tuple[Move, ...] = ()          # the venue's recent window (E16)
    deposits: tuple[Move, ...] = ()
    withdrawals: tuple[Move, ...] = ()
    withdrawal_addresses: tuple[Address, ...] = ()   # Upbit only
    key_expiry: str | None = None         # Upbit: earliest expire_at, model.iso_utc
    loans: Mapping[str, float] = field(default_factory=dict)         # name -> amount (E26)
    earn: Mapping[str, float] = field(default_factory=dict)          # OKX: name -> amount (E26)
    flags: frozenset = frozenset()        # subset of FLAGS
    prices_krw: Mapping[str, float] = field(default_factory=dict)    # symbol or currency -> KRW price used
    response_sha256: Mapping[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict) # path -> sha256 of the body; the OKX algo
                                          # calls use f"{path}?ordType={t}"; never a KIS query (E37)
    snapshot_sha256: str = ""             # set by __post_init__

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        object.__setattr__(self, "flags", frozenset(self.flags))     # a list or set hashes as the frozenset would
        if self.venue not in VENUES:
            raise ValueError("snapshot: venue is not kis, upbit or okx")
        if not self.flags <= FLAGS:
            raise ValueError("snapshot: a flag outside FLAGS")
        body = {k: v for k, v in model.jsonable(self).items() if k != "snapshot_sha256"}
        object.__setattr__(self, "snapshot_sha256", model.sha256_hex(model.canonical_json(body)))


_FIELDS = frozenset(f.name for f in dataclasses.fields(Snapshot))


def home() -> Path:
    """`<state root>/execution`, resolved at call time. Computing it creates nothing."""
    return state_root() / "execution"


def inquiry_path(day: date) -> Path:
    """The inquiry file of one Asia/Seoul date (E30): `inquiry-YYYYMMDD.jsonl`. Computing it creates nothing."""
    return home() / f"inquiry-{day:%Y%m%d}.jsonl"


def failed(venue: str, utc: str, error: str, *, flags=frozenset(), server_utc=None, clock_offset_s=None) -> Snapshot:
    """A not-ok snapshot: no holdings, cash or lists, only the error text (names, paths and codes, E37)."""
    return Snapshot(venue=venue, utc=utc, server_utc=server_utc, clock_offset_s=clock_offset_s, ok=False,
                    error=error, flags=flags)


def dump(snap: Snapshot) -> bytes:
    """One inquiry line: the canonical JSON of every field (keys sorted) plus a newline, UTF-8."""
    return (model.canonical_json(snap) + "\n").encode("utf-8")


def load(obj: dict) -> Snapshot:
    """The Snapshot a dump() line holds, nested records rebuilt. ValueError unless `obj` has exactly the snapshot
    fields, every record rebuilds, snapshot_sha256 recomputes (a tampered row) and `obj` is the row dump() writes for
    that Snapshot (a look-alike container is refused); the text names no value."""
    if not isinstance(obj, dict) or set(obj) != _FIELDS:
        raise ValueError("snapshot row: not the snapshot fields")
    try:
        snap = Snapshot(
            venue=obj["venue"], utc=obj["utc"], server_utc=obj["server_utc"], clock_offset_s=obj["clock_offset_s"],
            ok=obj["ok"], error=obj["error"],
            holdings={k: Holding(**v) for k, v in obj["holdings"].items()},
            cash=dict(obj["cash"]), deposit_krw=obj["deposit_krw"],
            open_orders=tuple(Order(**o) for o in obj["open_orders"]),
            fills=tuple(Move(**m) for m in obj["fills"]),
            deposits=tuple(Move(**m) for m in obj["deposits"]),
            withdrawals=tuple(Move(**m) for m in obj["withdrawals"]),
            withdrawal_addresses=tuple(Address(**a) for a in obj["withdrawal_addresses"]),
            key_expiry=obj["key_expiry"], loans=dict(obj["loans"]), earn=dict(obj["earn"]),
            flags=obj["flags"], prices_krw=dict(obj["prices_krw"]),
            response_sha256=dict(obj["response_sha256"]))
        same = json.loads(dump(snap)) == obj            # dict() and tuple() above also take "", [] or pairs
    except (TypeError, ValueError, AttributeError, RecursionError) as exc:   # json nests deeper than jsonable recurses
        raise ValueError(f"snapshot row: {type(exc).__name__}") from None
    if snap.snapshot_sha256 != obj["snapshot_sha256"]:
        raise ValueError("snapshot row: snapshot_sha256 does not recompute")
    if not same:
        raise ValueError("snapshot row: not canonical")
    return snap


# ponytail: one process-wide lock for every path, as owner._exclusive; nesting two exclusive() calls in one thread
# deadlocks (no caller nests them: poll.py takes poll.lock with its own code). Per-path locks if one ever must.
_LOCK = threading.Lock()


@contextlib.contextmanager
def exclusive(path: Path) -> Iterator[None]:
    """Serialise read-and-append on `path` across threads and processes: a sidecar `<path>.lock` holding an OS byte
    lock (a copy of core.compliance.owner._exclusive, which is private). Creates the folder and the lock file only."""
    checked_target(path.parent, "E1 state folder").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with _LOCK, open(checked_target(str(path) + ".lock", "E1 lock file"), "a+b") as fh:
        if os.name == "nt":
            import msvcrt
            fh.seek(0)
            msvcrt.locking(fh.fileno(), msvcrt.LK_LOCK, 1)       # retries for about 10 s, then raises
        else:
            import fcntl
            fcntl.flock(fh, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            if os.name == "nt":
                fh.seek(0)
                msvcrt.locking(fh.fileno(), msvcrt.LK_UNLCK, 1)
            else:
                fcntl.flock(fh, fcntl.LOCK_UN)


def write_lines(path: Path, lines: Sequence[bytes], what: str) -> None:
    """Append whole lines (each ending in a newline) to `path` with fsync; the caller holds exclusive(path) or, for
    the daily inquiry files, exclusive(home() / "inquiry"). A torn last line left by a crash stays isolated: a
    newline goes first when the file does not end in one. No lines: no file is opened or created."""
    if not lines:
        return
    with open(checked_target(path, what), "a+b") as fh:     # a+ reads the last byte; every write still appends
        end = fh.seek(0, os.SEEK_END)
        if end:
            fh.seek(end - 1)
            if fh.read(1) != b"\n":
                fh.write(b"\n")
        fh.write(b"".join(lines))
        fh.flush()
        os.fsync(fh.fileno())


def append_lines(path: Path, lines: Sequence[bytes], what: str) -> None:
    """write_lines under exclusive(path)."""
    with exclusive(path):
        write_lines(path, lines, what)


def read_all(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
    """Every JSON-object line of `path` in file order; a line that does not parse as one (a torn line, a foreign
    line, one nested too deep) is skipped; a missing file is []. Takes no lock and creates nothing."""
    try:
        with open(path, "rb") as fh:
            raw = fh.read()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return []
    rows = []
    for line in raw.split(b"\n"):
        try:
            obj = json.loads(line.decode("utf-8"))
        except (ValueError, RecursionError):            # UnicodeDecodeError and JSONDecodeError are ValueErrors
            continue
        if isinstance(obj, dict):
            rows.append(obj)
    return rows
```


  The two stat outputs must be identical (they catch a CR added to the modified fixtures file). They cannot catch a
  CRLF new file, since both count each of its lines as one insertion and .gitattributes (`* -text`) stores it as
  written; the `--eol` lines do. Each of the three lines must start with `i/lf    w/lf` (the rest is `attr/-text`
  and the path; git lists them sorted by path). Any other start (`i/crlf`, `i/mixed`) means stop: rewrite that file
  with LF endings using the Write tool, `git add` it again and repeat all three checks.

`tests/execution_acceptance.py` (Task 1) already lists `"execution_kis"` in MODULES and skips the module until this

from this task on they see its full text: the KIS token rule (every `/uapi/` string one of the nine GET paths), the
TR rule, the transport-only rule (one `keys.read(ACCOUNT_NAMES)`; every `request` call passes the literal `"GET"`),
the import allowlist and no clock. No CRLF file, no compliance file and no file outside the three above changes,
except the ledger line of a drift ruling.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes:
  - Task 2 (`execution/kis_inquiry.py`, contract 7): `ENDPOINTS`, `TR_IDS` (a frozenset of nine `(path, tr_id)`
    pairs, every TR id ending in R), `PUBLIC = frozenset()`, `ACCOUNT_NAMES = ("KIS_ACCOUNT_8", "KIS_ACCOUNT_PD")`.
  - Task 2 (`execution.keys`, contract 5): `read(names) -> tuple[str, ...]`, raising `KeyMissing(name)` (`.name` is
    the missing key's name; the message holds no value).
  - Tasks 2 and 3 (`execution.transport`, contract 6): `request(venue, method, path, params=None, *, tr_id=None) ->
    Answer` (`.body` the parsed JSON, `.server_utc` aware UTC from the Date header or None, `.received_utc`,
    `.sha256` hex over the raw body); `AuthError` (subclass of `InquiryError`), `InquiryError`, `InquiryRefused`,
    `KeyMissing` (re-exported from keys). Transport issues, caches and reuses the KIS token itself (one
    `POST /oauth2/tokenP` before the first GET when the cache in the state root holds no valid token), sends the

    `psbl_rvsecncl`, `nccs`, `ccnl`), `_routes(table, bodies, changes) -> dict` (Tasks 6 and 7 reuse it) and
    `kis_routes(**changes) -> dict`: `(method, path) -> answer` for `serve()` (contract 3.2; keyed as `serve()` takes
    them, so the three venues' routes merge with `|`), a fresh deep copy of each default answer, a keyword named
    after a `KIS_ROUTES` key replacing that answer with any `serve()` answer form, a None value dropping the route,
    an unknown name a `KeyError`.
  - Later users: Task 8 (`cash`, `holdings`, `prices_krw`), Task 10 (`deposit_krw`, `cash`, `prices_krw` of an ok
    KIS snapshot), Task 11 (`open_orders`, `fills`, `loans`, `flags`, `clock_offset_s`, the `code_unsigned` flag),

**Plan decisions used:** E42 and E24 (E1R2-9: KIS sends only under the poll's sealed, signed context), E14 (the
account number read only here, checked as 8 + 2 digits), E16 (D+2 cash, `deposit_krw`, the recent windows), E17
(US only, first page only; no rate, no price), E26 (the five KIS loan figures), E37 (error text from names only),
E38 (venue errors contained, nothing else), E39 (`clock_offset_s` at receipt), E10 and E36 (the allowlists stay in
this module; every `request` call passes the literal `"GET"`, and one `keys.read`), E15 (answers are checked in
transport), E2 (imports), E1R2-5 (`[assumed]` fixture fields accepted; a live mismatch fails KIS closed).

Design notes (read before Step 3):
- Contract 9 writes the gate's return through the module name, `snapshot.failed`; inside this module the function
  itself is named `snapshot`, so `failed` is imported from `execution.snapshot` and the gate reads
  `return failed("kis", model.iso_utc(now), "code not signed", flags=frozenset({"code_unsigned"}))`.
- The nine GETs go out in contract 9's order. The overseas cash answer (CTRP6504R) is parsed first because the
  overseas holdings' KRW prices need its rates; a holding whose currency has no rate gets no price, and positions then
  fail closed (E17).
- `_num` takes a string only (KIS sends every number as a string, contract 3.2): `""` is 0.0, commas are dropped
  (`"1,234,567"` is 1234567.0), and a JSON number, None, a bool, `"1,234,567KRW"`, `nan` or `inf` is
  `FieldError(name)`, whose text names the field and never the value (E37).
- A live mismatch fails KIS closed (E1R2-5) rather than passing as an odd value: every id, symbol and currency
  (`pdno`, `ovrs_pdno`, `crcy_cd`, `tr_crcy_cd`, `odno`, `ord_dt`) is read through `_text` (a non-empty string, else
  `FieldError(name)`), so no dict key is None or a number; `_holding` refuses an `ord_psbl_qty` below 0 or above the
  units held (`FieldError("ord_psbl_qty")`), so `locked` is never negative. `_side` keeps contract 9's mapping
  (`"01"` sell, anything else buy).
- A failed snapshot keeps the venue time read so far (`server_utc`, `clock_offset_s` from the answers already in),
  so CLOCK_SKEW still sees a poll that failed later (E39).
- The token POST is transport's: it is not in `answers`, so `response_sha256` and the venue time come from the nine
  GETs only. A test that removes `KIS_APP_KEY` runs last in its loop because that attempt starts transport's
  70-second issue gap (`_next_issue_at`, reset per test by `isolated()`).

```python
def _routes(table: dict, bodies: dict, changes: dict) -> dict:
    """{(method, path): answer} for serve(): a fresh deep copy of every default answer, or the change named after its
    route (any answer form serve() takes, used as given); a None change drops that route. An unknown name is a
    KeyError, so a typo cannot pass silently."""
    unknown = sorted(set(changes) - set(table))
    if unknown:
        raise KeyError(f"no such route: {unknown}")
    out = {}
    for name, route in table.items():
        answer = changes[name] if name in changes else copy.deepcopy(bodies[name])
        if answer is not None:
            out[route] = answer
    return out


def kis_routes(**changes) -> dict:
    """serve() routes for every KIS call, the token POST included, keyed (method, path) as serve() takes them, so the
    three venues' routes merge with `|`. A keyword named after a KIS_ROUTES key replaces that answer."""
    return _routes(KIS_ROUTES, KIS_BODIES, changes)
```

```python
"""KIS inquiry (E1 Task 5; contract C9; spec 5 KIS, 6; E14, E16, E17, E26, E37, E38, E39, E42).

Every send goes to `EF.serve` (the KIS answers of contract 3.2, never a live one); the suite's wrapper refuses any
other send. Every ok case passes `F.ctx()` (sealed, `code_signed=True`): KIS sends nothing under unsigned code.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import ast
import dataclasses
import hashlib
import json
import re
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

from core.compliance import model
from execution import keys, kis_inquiry, transport
from execution.snapshot import Holding, Move, Order
from tests import compliance_fixtures as F
from tests import execution_fixtures as EF

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
PATH = {name: route[1] for name, route in EF.KIS_ROUTES.items()}
GETS = ("balance", "psbl_rvsecncl", "daily_ccld", "account_balance", "intgr_margin", "ovrs_balance", "nccs", "ccnl",
        "present_balance")                          # the order of contract C9
ACCOUNT_ERROR = "kis: KIS account number is not 8 + 2 digits"


def _path(call: dict) -> str:
    return urlsplit(call["url"]).path


def _pairs(call: dict) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """The sent query as (key, value) pairs, exactly as on the wire (not unquoted)."""
    return [tuple(p.split("=", 1)) for p in urlsplit(call["url"]).query.split("&")]


def _only(calls: list, name: str) -> dict:
    found = [c for c in calls if _path(c) == PATH[name]]
    assert len(found) == 1, (name, len(found))
    return found[0]


def _full() -> dict:
    """kis_routes() with one row in each list the defaults leave empty."""
    routes = EF.kis_routes()
    for name in ("psbl_rvsecncl", "nccs", "ccnl"):
        routes[EF.KIS_ROUTES[name]]["output"] = [dict(EF.KIS_ROWS[name])]
    return routes


def _run(routes: dict, ctx=None, **key_changes):
    """One snapshot at EF.NOW under the fake keys (a keyword changes one; None removes it); (snapshot, calls)."""
    with EF.fake_keys(**key_changes), EF.serve(routes) as calls:
        snap = kis_inquiry.snapshot(EF.NOW, F.ctx() if ctx is None else ctx)
    return snap, calls


def _no_key_read(names):
    raise AssertionError(f"keys.read({tuple(names)}) under unsigned code")


def _names_only(error: str) -> bool:
    """True when a failure text holds neither the fake account number nor the account field (E37)."""
    return EF.FAKE_KEYS["KIS_ACCOUNT_8"] not in error and "CANO" not in error


def test_the_signed_code_gate_is_the_first_statement():
    tree = ast.parse((ROOT / "execution" / "kis_inquiry.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    fn = next((n for n in tree.body if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef) and n.name == "snapshot"), None)
    assert fn is not None, "kis_inquiry.snapshot is not defined"
    body = fn.body[1:] if ast.get_docstring(fn) else fn.body
    gate = body[0]
    assert isinstance(gate, ast.If) and not gate.orelse, ast.unparse(gate)
    assert ast.unparse(gate.test) == "not (model.is_sealed(ctx) and ctx.code_signed is True)", ast.unparse(gate.test)
    assert [ast.unparse(s) for s in gate.body] == [
        "return failed('kis', model.iso_utc(now), 'code not signed', flags=frozenset({'code_unsigned'}))"]


def test_kis_sends_nothing_and_reads_no_key_unless_the_code_is_signed():
    unsealed = dataclasses.replace(F.ctx())
    assert not model.is_sealed(unsealed)
    for ctx in (F.ctx(code_signed=False), F.ctx(code_signed=1), unsealed, None):
        saved = keys.read
        keys.read = _no_key_read
        try:
            with EF.fake_keys(), EF.serve(_full()) as calls:
                snap = kis_inquiry.snapshot(EF.NOW, ctx)
        finally:
            keys.read = saved
        assert calls == [], [_path(c) for c in calls]                # not even the token POST
        assert not snap.ok and snap.error == "code not signed", snap.error
        assert snap.flags == frozenset({"code_unsigned"}) and snap.utc == "2026-10-24T00:00:00Z"
        assert snap.holdings == {} and snap.response_sha256 == {} and snap.server_utc is None
    snap, calls = _run(_full())
    assert snap.ok and snap.error is None and len(calls) == 10, snap.error   # signed: the token POST and nine GETs


def test_the_full_fixture_gives_every_field():
    snap, _calls = _run(_full())
    assert snap.ok and snap.error is None and snap.flags == frozenset(), snap.error
    assert snap.venue == "kis" and snap.utc == "2026-10-24T00:00:00Z"
    assert snap.server_utc == "2026-10-24T00:00:00Z" and snap.clock_offset_s == 0.0
    assert dict(snap.holdings) == {"005930": Holding(units=1.0, locked=0.0, avg_cost=60000.0),
                                   "AAPL": Holding(units=1.0, locked=0.0, avg_cost=200.0)}
    assert dict(snap.cash) == {"KRW": 20000.0, "USD": 5.0}       # KRW: the D+2 prvs_rcdl_excc_amt, not dnca_tot_amt
    assert snap.deposit_krw == 21000.0                           # dnca_tot_amt (D16 evidence)
    assert dict(snap.prices_krw) == {"005930": 61000.0, "AAPL": 210.0 * 1390.5, "USD": 1390.5}
    assert snap.open_orders == (Order(id="0000123456", symbol="005930", side="buy", units=1.0, price=60000.0),
                                Order(id="0000223456", symbol="AAPL", side="buy", units=1.0, price=200.0))
    assert snap.fills == (Move(id="20261023-0000123455", symbol="005930", counter="KRW", side="buy", units=1.0),
                          Move(id="20261023-0000223455", symbol="AAPL", counter="USD", side="buy", units=1.0))
    assert dict(snap.loans) == {"tot_loan_amt": 0.0, "loan_amt": 0.0, "crdt_fncg_amt": 0.0, "thdt_rcvb_amt": 0.0,
                                "rcvb_amt": 0.0}
    assert snap.deposits == () and snap.withdrawals == () and snap.withdrawal_addresses == ()
    assert snap.key_expiry is None and dict(snap.earn) == {}
    assert set(snap.response_sha256) == {PATH[n] for n in GETS}  # one per path, no query (it holds the account)
    assert all("?" not in k for k in snap.response_sha256)
    assert all(re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", v) for v in snap.response_sha256.values())


def test_every_call_is_a_get_with_its_pinned_tr_and_the_account_from_keys():
    reads, saved = [], keys.read

    def recording(names):
        reads.append(tuple(names))
        return saved(names)
    keys.read = recording
    try:
        snap, calls = _run(EF.kis_routes(), KIS_ACCOUNT_8="97654310", KIS_ACCOUNT_PD="37")
    finally:
        keys.read = saved
    assert snap.ok, snap.error
    assert reads[0] == ("KIS_ACCOUNT_8", "KIS_ACCOUNT_PD") == kis_inquiry.ACCOUNT_NAMES      # before any request
    assert reads.count(kis_inquiry.ACCOUNT_NAMES) == 1
    assert [(c["method"], _path(c)) for c in calls] == [("POST", "/oauth2/tokenP")] + [("GET", PATH[n]) for n in GETS]
    pinned = dict(kis_inquiry.TR_IDS)
    for call in calls[1:]:
        assert call["headers"]["tr_id"] == pinned[_path(call)] and call["headers"]["tr_id"].endswith("R")
        assert _pairs(call)[:2] == [("CANO", "97654310"), ("ACNT_PRDT_CD", "37")], _pairs(call)[:2]
    balance = _pairs(_only(calls, "balance"))
    assert ("INQR_DVSN", "01") in balance and [k for k, _v in balance].count("INQR_DVSN") == 1
    ccnl = _pairs(_only(calls, "ccnl"))
    assert ("PDNO", "%25") in ccnl                               # "%" goes out as %25
    assert ("OVRS_EXCG_CD", "NASD") in ccnl and ("TR_CRCY_CD", "USD") in _pairs(_only(calls, "ovrs_balance"))


def test_the_dates_are_seoul_dates():
    for now, d0, d1, d2 in ((datetime(2026, 10, 23, 14, 59, 59, tzinfo=timezone.utc), "20261023", "20261022",
                             "20261021"),
                            (datetime(2026, 10, 23, 15, 0, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc), "20261024", "20261023",
                             "20261022")):

        daily, ccnl = _pairs(_only(calls, "daily_ccld")), _pairs(_only(calls, "ccnl"))
        assert ("INQR_STRT_DT", d1) in daily and ("INQR_END_DT", d0) in daily, daily
        assert ("ORD_STRT_DT", d2) in ccnl and ("ORD_END_DT", d0) in ccnl, ccnl


def test_server_time_and_offset_come_from_the_first_answer_with_a_date_header():
    no_date = json.dumps(EF.KIS_BODIES["balance"]).encode("utf-8")
    later = json.dumps(EF.KIS_BODIES["present_balance"]).encode("utf-8")
    routes = EF.kis_routes(balance=lambda call: (200, {}, no_date),
                           present_balance=lambda call: (200, {"Date": "Sat, 24 Oct 2026 00:00:45 GMT"}, later))
    with EF.fake_keys(), EF.serve(routes, date="Sat, 24 Oct 2026 00:00:30 GMT"):

    fills = routes[EF.KIS_ROUTES["daily_ccld"]]["output1"]

    assert snap.open_orders == (Order(id="0000123456", symbol="005930", side="sell", units=1.0, price=60000.0),

def test_a_missing_or_malformed_field_fails_closed_with_its_name():
    cases = (("balance", lambda b: b["output2"][0].pop("prvs_rcdl_excc_amt"), "prvs_rcdl_excc_amt"),
             ("present_balance", lambda b: b["output2"][0].pop("crcy_cd"), "crcy_cd"),
             ("intgr_margin", lambda b: b.pop("output"), "output"),
             ("daily_ccld", lambda b: b["output1"][0].pop("ord_dt"), "ord_dt"),
             ("ovrs_balance", lambda b: b.update(output1={}), "output1"),
             ("account_balance", lambda b: b.update(output2=[]), "output2"),
             # the field each value comes from, where the fixture gives a sibling field the same value
             ("present_balance", lambda b: b["output2"][0].pop("frcr_dncl_amt_2"), "frcr_dncl_amt_2"),
             ("ovrs_balance", lambda b: b["output1"][0].pop("now_pric2"), "now_pric2"),
             ("ovrs_balance", lambda b: b["output1"][0].pop("pchs_avg_pric"), "pchs_avg_pric"),
             ("nccs", lambda b: b["output"][0].pop("nccs_qty"), "nccs_qty"),
             ("ccnl", lambda b: b["output"][0].pop("tr_crcy_cd"), "tr_crcy_cd"),
             # a live mismatch fails closed (E1R2-5): more free than held, less than none, an id that is not text
             ("balance", lambda b: b["output1"][0].update(ord_psbl_qty="2"), "ord_psbl_qty"),
             ("ovrs_balance", lambda b: b["output1"][0].update(ord_psbl_qty="-1"), "ord_psbl_qty"),
             ("balance", lambda b: b["output1"][0].update(pdno=""), "pdno"),
             ("ccnl", lambda b: b["output"][0].update(odno=223455), "odno"))
    for name, change, field in cases:
        routes = _full()
        change(routes[EF.KIS_ROUTES[name]])
        snap, _calls = _run(routes)
        assert not snap.ok and snap.flags == frozenset(), (name, field)
        assert snap.error == f"kis: {PATH[name]}: field {field}", snap.error


def test_a_malformed_number_fails_closed_without_its_value():

def test_a_refused_send_propagates():
    with EF.fake_keys():
        try:
            kis_inquiry.snapshot(EF.NOW, F.ctx())                # no serve(): the suite's refusing stub answers
        except EF.Refused:
            pass
        else:
            raise AssertionError("a refused send became a snapshot")
    assert len(EF.STRAYS) == 1, EF.STRAYS                         # the token POST, refused
    EF.STRAYS.clear()


def test_a_refused_write_propagates():
    def refuse(path, what="path", **kw):
        raise RuntimeError(f"{what} refused (test)")
    saved = transport.checked_target
    transport.checked_target = refuse
    try:
        with EF.fake_keys(), EF.serve(EF.kis_routes()) as calls:
            kis_inquiry.snapshot(EF.NOW, F.ctx())
    except RuntimeError as exc:
        assert "refused (test)" in str(exc) and calls == [], calls   # refused before the token POST, not contained
    else:
        raise AssertionError("a refused write became a snapshot")
    finally:
        transport.checked_target = saved
```

  from the first character through the end of the line `from __future__ import annotations` as old_string (Step 1
  already showed that only the docstring and that line sit above the constants), and record a one-line ruling in the

```python
"""KIS read-only inquiry (E1 spec 5 and 6; plan C7, C9): the frozen allowlist, the pinned TR ids and the KIS snapshot
of one poll. The only E1 file that names the KIS account fields. A KIS key can also trade, so `snapshot` reads no
key and sends nothing unless the poll's sealed context says the code on disk is the code the owner signed (E42).
Every list is read on its first page only."""
from __future__ import annotations

import math
from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta

from core.compliance import model
from execution import keys
from execution.snapshot import FieldError, Holding, Move, Order, Snapshot, failed
from execution.transport import AuthError, InquiryError, InquiryRefused, KeyMissing, request
```

  Edit 3b, anchor: the last constant line. old_string:

```python
ACCOUNT_NAMES = ("KIS_ACCOUNT_8", "KIS_ACCOUNT_PD")
```

  new_string (that line, one blank line, then the snapshot and its helpers):

```python
ACCOUNT_NAMES = ("KIS_ACCOUNT_8", "KIS_ACCOUNT_PD")

_BALANCE = "/uapi/domestic-stock/v1/trading/inquire-balance"
_OPEN = "/uapi/domestic-stock/v1/trading/inquire-psbl-rvsecncl"
_FILLS = "/uapi/domestic-stock/v1/trading/inquire-daily-ccld"
_ASSETS = "/uapi/domestic-stock/v1/trading/inquire-account-balance"
_MARGIN = "/uapi/domestic-stock/v1/trading/intgr-margin"
_US_BALANCE = "/uapi/overseas-stock/v1/trading/inquire-balance"
_US_OPEN = "/uapi/overseas-stock/v1/trading/inquire-nccs"
_US_FILLS = "/uapi/overseas-stock/v1/trading/inquire-ccnl"
_US_CASH = "/uapi/overseas-stock/v1/trading/inquire-present-balance"
_CONTAINED = (KeyMissing, InquiryRefused, InquiryError, LookupError, ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError,
              ArithmeticError)                      # E38: the venue's own errors (AuthError and FieldError included)


def snapshot(now: datetime, ctx: model.Context) -> Snapshot:
    """The KIS snapshot of the poll at `now` (C9); `ctx` is the context that poll loaded first (E24). A venue error
    gives a failed snapshot whose text holds names, paths and codes only (E37, E38); a refused write, the suite's
    refusing stub and a programming error propagate."""
    if not (model.is_sealed(ctx) and ctx.code_signed is True):
        return failed("kis", model.iso_utc(now), "code not signed", flags=frozenset({"code_unsigned"}))
    utc, path, answers = model.iso_utc(now), "", {}
    try:
        cano, prdt = keys.read(ACCOUNT_NAMES)
        if not (_digits(cano, 8) and _digits(prdt, 2)):
            return failed("kis", utc, "kis: KIS account number is not 8 + 2 digits")
        pinned = dict(TR_IDS)
        # ponytail: first page only; a 51st holding or 101st fill is missed; add tr_cont paging when the account grows
        for path, params in _calls(cano, prdt, now.astimezone(model.KST).date()):
            answers[path] = request("kis", "GET", path, params, tr_id=pinned[path])
        body = {p: a.body for p, a in answers.items()}
        path, cash, prices, rates = _US_CASH, {}, {}, {}    # first: the overseas prices need its rates
        for row in _list(body[path], "output2"):
            ccy = _text(row, "crcy_cd")
            cash[ccy] = _num(row, "frcr_dncl_amt_2")
            rates[ccy] = prices[ccy] = _num(row, "frst_bltn_exrt")
        path, holdings = _BALANCE, {}
        rows, total = _list(body[path], "output1"), _one(body[path], "output2")
        cash["KRW"] = _num(total, "prvs_rcdl_excc_amt")     # D+2: a buy not yet settled is not counted twice (E16)
        deposit = _num(total, "dnca_tot_amt")
        loans = {"tot_loan_amt": _num(total, "tot_loan_amt"),
                 "loan_amt": sum((_num(r, "loan_amt") for r in rows), 0.0)}
        for row in rows:
            units = _num(row, "hldg_qty")
            if units > 0:
                holdings[_text(row, "pdno")] = _holding(row, units)
                prices[_text(row, "pdno")] = _num(row, "prpr")
        path = _US_BALANCE
        for row in _list(body[path], "output1"):
            units = _num(row, "ovrs_cblc_qty")
            if units > 0:
                symbol, rate = _text(row, "ovrs_pdno"), rates.get(_text(row, "tr_crcy_cd"))
                holdings[symbol] = _holding(row, units)
                if rate is not None:                        # no rate, no price: positions then fail closed (E17)
                    prices[symbol] = _num(row, "now_pric2") * rate
        path, orders = _OPEN, []
        for row in _list(body[path], "output"):
            units = _num(row, "psbl_qty")
            if units > 0:
                orders.append(Order(id=_text(row, "odno"), symbol=_text(row, "pdno"), side=_side(row), units=units,
                                    price=_num(row, "ord_unpr")))
        path = _US_OPEN
        for row in _list(body[path], "output"):
            orders.append(Order(id=_text(row, "odno"), symbol=_text(row, "pdno"), side=_side(row),
                                units=_num(row, "nccs_qty") or _num(row, "ft_ord_qty"),
                                price=_num(row, "ft_ord_unpr3")))
        fills = []
        for path, rows_name, units_name in ((_FILLS, "output1", "tot_ccld_qty"), (_US_FILLS, "output", "ft_ccld_qty")):
            for row in _list(body[path], rows_name):
                units = _num(row, units_name)
                if units > 0:
                    counter = "KRW" if path == _FILLS else _text(row, "tr_crcy_cd")
                    fills.append(Move(id=f"{_text(row, 'ord_dt')}-{_text(row, 'odno')}", symbol=_text(row, "pdno"),
                                      counter=counter, side=_side(row), units=units))
        path = _ASSETS
        assets = _one(body[path], "output2")
        loans["crdt_fncg_amt"] = _num(assets, "crdt_fncg_amt")
        loans["thdt_rcvb_amt"] = _num(assets, "thdt_rcvb_amt")
        path = _MARGIN
        loans["rcvb_amt"] = _num(_one(body[path], "output"), "rcvb_amt")
        server_utc, offset = _clock_of(answers)
        return Snapshot(venue="kis", utc=utc, server_utc=server_utc, clock_offset_s=offset, ok=True,
                        holdings=holdings, cash=cash, deposit_krw=deposit, open_orders=tuple(orders),
                        fills=tuple(fills), loans=loans, prices_krw=prices,
                        response_sha256={p: a.sha256 for p, a in answers.items()})   # paths only, never a query
    except _CONTAINED as exc:
        return _failed(utc, path, exc, answers)


def _calls(cano: str, prdt: str, today: date) -> tuple[tuple[str, list[tuple[str, str]]], ...]:
    """(path, params) of the nine GETs in their order (C9); the dates are Seoul dates."""
    d0, d1, d2 = (f"{today - timedelta(days=n):%Y%m%d}" for n in (0, 1, 2))
    acct = [("CANO", cano), ("ACNT_PRDT_CD", prdt)]
    return (
        (_BALANCE, acct + [("AFHR_FLPR_YN", "N"), ("OFL_YN", ""), ("INQR_DVSN", "01"), ("UNPR_DVSN", "01"),
                           ("FUND_STTL_ICLD_YN", "N"), ("FNCG_AMT_AUTO_RDPT_YN", "N"), ("PRCS_DVSN", "00"),
                           ("CTX_AREA_FK100", ""), ("CTX_AREA_NK100", "")]),
        (_OPEN, acct + [("CTX_AREA_FK100", ""), ("CTX_AREA_NK100", ""), ("INQR_DVSN_1", "0"),
                        ("INQR_DVSN_2", "0")]),
        (_FILLS, acct + [("INQR_STRT_DT", d1), ("INQR_END_DT", d0), ("SLL_BUY_DVSN_CD", "00"), ("INQR_DVSN", "00"),
                         ("PDNO", ""), ("CCLD_DVSN", "01"), ("ORD_GNO_BRNO", ""), ("ODNO", ""),
                         ("INQR_DVSN_3", "00"), ("INQR_DVSN_1", ""), ("EXCG_ID_DVSN_CD", "ALL"),
                         ("CTX_AREA_FK100", ""), ("CTX_AREA_NK100", "")]),
        (_ASSETS, acct + [("INQR_DVSN_1", ""), ("BSPR_BF_DT_APLY_YN", "")]),
        (_MARGIN, acct + [("CMA_EVLU_AMT_ICLD_YN", "N"), ("WCRC_FRCR_DVSN_CD", "01"),
                          ("FWEX_CTRT_FRCR_DVSN_CD", "01")]),
        (_US_BALANCE, acct + [("OVRS_EXCG_CD", "NASD"), ("TR_CRCY_CD", "USD"), ("CTX_AREA_FK200", ""),
                              ("CTX_AREA_NK200", "")]),
        (_US_OPEN, acct + [("OVRS_EXCG_CD", "NASD"), ("SORT_SQN", "DS"), ("CTX_AREA_FK200", ""),
                           ("CTX_AREA_NK200", "")]),
        (_US_FILLS, acct + [("PDNO", "%"), ("ORD_STRT_DT", d2), ("ORD_END_DT", d0), ("SLL_BUY_DVSN", "00"),
                            ("CCLD_NCCS_DVSN", "01"), ("OVRS_EXCG_CD", "NASD"), ("SORT_SQN", "DS"), ("ORD_DT", ""),
                            ("ORD_GNO_BRNO", ""), ("ODNO", ""), ("CTX_AREA_NK200", ""), ("CTX_AREA_FK200", "")]),
        (_US_CASH, acct + [("WCRC_FRCR_DVSN_CD", "02"), ("NATN_CD", "000"), ("TR_MKET_CD", "00"),
                           ("INQR_DVSN_CD", "00")]),
    )


def _failed(utc: str, path: str, exc: Exception, answers: dict) -> Snapshot:
    """A contained venue error as a failed snapshot (E38), keeping the venue time read so far (E39); the text is
    built from names only, never str() of a parse or network error (E37)."""
    if isinstance(exc, KeyMissing):
        error, flags = f"keys missing: {exc.name}", frozenset({"keys_missing"})
    elif isinstance(exc, AuthError):
        error, flags = str(exc), frozenset({"auth_error"})
    elif isinstance(exc, (InquiryRefused, InquiryError)):
        error, flags = str(exc), frozenset()
    elif isinstance(exc, FieldError):
        error, flags = f"kis: {path}: field {exc.args[0]}", frozenset()
    else:
        error, flags = f"kis: {path}: {type(exc).__name__}", frozenset()
    server_utc, offset = _clock_of(answers)
    return failed("kis", utc, error, flags=flags, server_utc=server_utc, clock_offset_s=offset)


def _clock_of(answers: dict) -> tuple[str | None, float | None]:
    """server_utc and clock_offset_s from the first answer with a Date header (E39)."""
    for answer in answers.values():
        if answer.server_utc is not None:
            return model.iso_utc(answer.server_utc), (answer.server_utc - answer.received_utc).total_seconds()
    return None, None


def _field(row, name: str):
    """row[name]; FieldError(name) when row is not a dict or lacks it (E37)."""
    if not isinstance(row, dict) or name not in row:
        raise FieldError(name)
    return row[name]


def _text(row, name: str) -> str:
    """row[name] as a non-empty string (an id, a symbol, a currency or a date); otherwise FieldError(name)."""
    value = _field(row, name)
    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
        raise FieldError(name)
    return value


def _num(row, name: str) -> float:
    """A finite number from a KIS string ("" is 0, commas dropped); otherwise FieldError(name), never the value."""
    value = _field(row, name)
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        raise FieldError(name)
    try:
        number = 0.0 if value == "" else float(value.replace(",", ""))
    except ValueError:
        raise FieldError(name) from None
    if not math.isfinite(number):
        raise FieldError(name)
    return number


def _one(body, name: str) -> dict:
    """body[name] as one dict: the dict itself, or the first row of a non-empty list."""
    value = _field(body, name)
    if isinstance(value, list) and value:
        value = value[0]
    if not isinstance(value, dict):
        raise FieldError(name)
    return value


def _list(body, name: str) -> list:
    """body[name], which must be a list."""
    rows = _field(body, name)
    if not isinstance(rows, list):
        raise FieldError(name)
    return rows


def _side(row) -> str:
    return "sell" if _field(row, "sll_buy_dvsn_cd") == "01" else "buy"


def _holding(row, units: float) -> Holding:
    free = _num(row, "ord_psbl_qty")
    if not 0.0 <= free <= units:                    # more free than held is a field mismatch: fail closed (E1R2-5)
        raise FieldError("ord_psbl_qty")
    return Holding(units=units, locked=units - free, avg_cost=_num(row, "pchs_avg_pric"))


def _digits(value: str, n: int) -> bool:
    return len(value) == n and value.isascii() and value.isdigit()
```

  Write `canonical` in lower case if you touch a docstring or comment (the upper-case word holds the account-field
  text), and keep every `/uapi/` string exactly one of the nine paths with no punctuation after it in a comment (the
  KIS token rule reads comments too).

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes:
  - Task 2 (`execution/upbit_inquiry.py`, contract 7): `ENDPOINTS` (nine `("GET", path)` pairs, `/v1/status/wallet`
    included), `PUBLIC = frozenset({"/v1/ticker"})`.

    Answer` (`.body`, `.server_utc`, `.received_utc`, `.sha256`); `AuthError`, `InquiryError`, `InquiryRefused`,
    `KeyMissing`. Transport signs every Upbit path but `/v1/ticker` with an HS512 JWT
    (`Authorization: Bearer <jwt>`, payload `access_key`, a fresh `nonce`, and `query_hash` = SHA512 hex of the
    exact query on the wire plus `query_hash_alg: "SHA512"` when there is one; no `exp`), reads the Upbit keys only
    for a signed call (a missing one raises `KeyMissing` before anything is sent), refuses a signed value that
    quoting would change, raises `AuthError` on HTTP 401/403 or an error name in `AUTH_CODES["upbit"]`
    (`out_of_scope` included), raises `InquiryError` naming venue, path, HTTP status and code (never the venue's
    message) on any other error answer (E15), and lets the router's `AssertionError` through unchanged.
  - Task 4 (`execution.snapshot`): `Address(currency, net_type, address, secondary_address="")`, `FieldError`,

  - Tests: Tasks 1 to 4 fixtures as in Task 5 (`NOW`, `DATE_HEADER`, `FAKE_KEYS` with `UPBIT_ACCESS_KEY`
    `"test-upbit-access"` and `UPBIT_SECRET_KEY` `"test-upbit-secret"`, `Refused`, `STRAYS` (`"METHOD url-path"`
    rows), `fake_keys`, `serve` (an unrouted call appends to `STRAYS` and raises `AssertionError`)); Task 5's
    `_routes(table, bodies, changes)` (a None change drops that route).
- Produces:
  - `execution/upbit_inquiry.py`: `snapshot(now: datetime) -> Snapshot`. It sends, in this order, the signed GETs
    `/v1/accounts`, `/v1/orders/open` (`states[]=wait&states[]=watch&limit=100`), `/v1/orders/closed`
    (`states[]=done&states[]=cancel&limit=1000`, no time: Upbit's default 7 days), `/v1/withdraws` (`limit=100`),
    `/v1/withdraws/coin_addresses`, `/v1/deposits` (`limit=100`), `/v1/api_keys`, then the public `/v1/ticker`
    with `markets` = the sorted `KRW-<coin>` of every held coin plus `KRW-USDT`. It never calls `/v1/status/wallet`
    (E22). The ok snapshot holds `cash = {"KRW": balance + locked}`, `holdings` (every other currency with
    `balance + locked > 0`: `Holding(units=balance + locked, locked=locked, avg_cost=avg_buy_price if unit_currency
    == "KRW" else None)`), `open_orders` (`Order(id=uuid, symbol=<base>, side="buy" for bid else "sell",
    units=remaining_volume, price=price or None)`), `fills` (closed rows with `executed_volume > 0`:
    `Move(id=uuid, symbol=<base>, counter=<quote>, side, units=executed_volume)`), `withdrawals` (`side="out"`),
    `deposits` (`side="in"`), `withdrawal_addresses` (`Address(currency, net_type, address=withdraw_address,
    secondary_address=secondary_address or "")`), `key_expiry` (the earliest `expire_at` of every listed key, an
    offset-less value read as Asia/Seoul, then `model.iso_utc`; None when none is listed; E21), `prices_krw`
    (`<base> -> trade_price` of each `KRW-<base>` ticker row, `USDT` included: Task 12 passes it to OKX; a row
    quoted in anything but KRW is `FieldError("market")`), `server_utc` and `clock_offset_s` from the first answer
    with a Date header, and `response_sha256` keyed by the eight paths. Venue errors fail the snapshot as in Task 5
    (`upbit: <path>: field <name>`, `upbit: <path>: <TypeName>`, `keys missing: <name>` with `keys_missing`,
    `str(exc)` with `auth_error` for an `AuthError`, `str(exc)` with no flag for any other `InquiryError` or an
    `InquiryRefused`), and a failed snapshot keeps the venue time read before the failure (E39); anything else
    propagates, the router's `AssertionError` and the suite's `Refused` included (E38).
  - Private to `execution/upbit_inquiry.py`: the path constants `_ACCOUNTS`, `_OPEN`, `_CLOSED`, `_WITHDRAWS`,
    `_ADDRESSES`, `_DEPOSITS`, `_KEYS`, `_TICKER`; `_SIGNED` (the seven signed calls and their parameters);
    `_CONTAINED`; `_failed`, `_clock_of`, `_rows(body)` (an Upbit list answer, else `FieldError("body")`),
    `_field`, `_num` (a decimal string or a JSON number, never a bool, nan, inf or a number too large for a float),
    `_price`, `_market(row) -> (quote, base)` (else `FieldError("market")`), `_side`, `_when(row, name) -> datetime`.
  - `tests/execution_fixtures.py`: `UPBIT_ROUTES`, `UPBIT_BODIES`, `UPBIT_ROWS` (an open order, a withdrawal, the
    offset-less key `api_keys_naive`, the `out_of_scope` error body) and `upbit_routes(**changes) -> dict`:
    `(method, path) -> answer` for `serve()`, as `kis_routes()`; a keyword named after an `UPBIT_ROUTES` key replaces
    that answer (None drops it); the routes include `/v1/status/wallet` so a test can show it is never asked.
  - Later users: Task 8 (`cash`, `holdings`, `prices_krw`), Task 11 (`key_expiry`, `withdrawal_addresses`,
    `open_orders`, `fills`, `deposits`, `withdrawals`, `clock_offset_s`, `auth_error`, `keys_missing`), Task 12
    (`poll_once` asks Upbit first and passes `prices_krw.get("USDT")` of an ok Upbit snapshot to OKX, E32).

**Plan decisions used:** E12 (the query built once and hashed as sent), E16 (KRW is settled cash, coins are
holdings, the 7-day and latest-100 windows), E21 (key expiry is the earliest of all listed keys), E22 (the wallet
status is allowlisted and never called), E37, E38, E39, E10 and E36 (every `request` call passes the literal
`"GET"`; the four exact Upbit paths only here), E2, E1R2-5.

Design notes (read before Step 3):
- Upbit answers lists; exchange numbers are decimal strings and quotation prices JSON numbers (contract 3.2), so
  this module's `_num` takes both and refuses a bool, `nan`, `inf`, a number too large for a float and any other
  type; an answer that is not a list is `FieldError("body")`.
- `/v1/api_keys` lists every key of the account and E1 never sees its own key's value outside transport, so
  `key_expiry` is the earliest `expire_at` of all of them (E21).
- The ticker is asked last, after the balances: its `markets` come from the held coins. `KRW-USDT` is always asked,
  since OKX values USDT, USDC and BTC with it (E32). Only KRW markets are asked, so a ticker row in any other quote
  is a venue anomaly and fails the snapshot (`prices_krw` must hold KRW prices only).

```python
    "orders_open": {"uuid": "u-open-1", "side": "bid", "ord_type": "limit", "price": "90000000", "state": "wait",
                    "market": "KRW-BTC", "created_at": "2026-10-24T08:55:00+09:00", "volume": "0.0001",
                    "remaining_volume": "0.0001", "executed_volume": "0", "trades_count": 0},
    "withdraws": {"type": "withdraw", "uuid": "u-wd-1", "currency": "BTC", "net_type": "BTC", "txid": "t1",

    "out_of_scope": {"error": {"name": "out_of_scope", "message": "fixture: the key lacks this permission"}},

def upbit_routes(**changes) -> dict:
    """serve() routes for every Upbit call (the never-called /v1/status/wallet included), keyed (method, path); a
    keyword named after an UPBIT_ROUTES key replaces that answer (None drops it)."""
    return _routes(UPBIT_ROUTES, UPBIT_BODIES, changes)
```
